title: Canonical Lico Arc Product Scope
goal: Converge Lico Arc on the exact local-first foundations and scenarios, keep LicoLite collaboration optional and manually installed, and require direct per-operation approval for every external transfer of user or client information.
description: Upper product constraint for every active plan: Rust local task queue, ACP, MCP, five platform adapters, local-agent discovery/conversation/skills/conversation-backup/usage, Secure Client Mesh mobile relay, optional user-installed LicoLite collaboration plugins, scoped regression, privacy, rebuild and launch.

title: Local Agent Execution and Orchestration
goal: Deliver real realtime exact-session forwarding for every canonical local agent plus deterministic multi-agent routing, protected path-based context transfer, framework compression, and dynamically reloadable adapter configuration.
description: Platform-neutral client capability plan and single current authority for local-agent execution, adapter lifecycle, context preparation, orchestration scheduling, GUI/CLI integration, and capability evidence; release consumes its final receipt.

title: LicoArc End-to-End Release
goal: Converge every current client plan and every freshly proven blocker into one source-controlled contract with truthful GitHub Releases, separately reported platform/store channels, and a separately gated product-line security claim.
description: Platform-neutral parent plan for product behavior, security, quality, evidence, and exact-artifact contracts consumed by the five platform release children.

title: Secure Mesh Local Security Provider Foundation
goal: Deliver one user-authorized, privacy-minimal, platform-neutral provider foundation that lets developers adapt trusted local key tools without remote executable code or silent wire-protocol changes.
description: Platform-neutral child of client-release for provider ports, protocol-owned operation context, local measurement, authorization, developer extension packages, session pinning, and conformance tooling. Concrete providers become nested children when real; existing platform release siblings consume redacted receipts.

title: macOS Release
goal: Produce and consumer-verify each declared macOS GitHub Release artifact through one digest-bound lineage while reporting Developer ID or App Store readiness separately when requested.
description: macOS child of the shared release contract; owns Keychain authorization, target-specific bundles, exact-artifact verification, and optional Developer ID/App Store channel evidence.

title: Android Release
goal: Produce a deterministic, consumer-verifiable Android arm64 GitHub Release artifact; evaluate user-authorized native custody plus physical install and launch only in the separate product-line security verdict, and report store continuity separately when requested.
description: Android child of the shared release contract; owns Keystore and BiometricPrompt policy, APK lineage, authorized-device evidence, exact-artifact verification, and optional store-channel status.

title: Linux Release
goal: Produce each declared Linux tuple through one consumer-verifiable artifact path with truthful custody, bounded smoke, installation, and launch evidence; report publisher-channel status separately when requested.
description: Linux child of the shared release contract; owns glibc and musl target lineages, Secret Service or memory-only custody, VM evidence, exact-artifact verification, and optional registry-channel status.

title: iOS Release
goal: Replace the declared iOS builder and evidence gaps with a consumer-verifiable arm64 client, native custody and FFI proof, physical launch, and Secure Mesh acceptance; report Apple channel status separately when requested.
description: iOS child of the shared release contract; remains fail-closed for unsupported build and security claims until its builder, LocalAuthentication/Keychain bridge, and physical evidence are complete; TestFlight/App Store readiness is independent guidance.

title: Windows Release
goal: Produce independently consumer-verified Windows x64 and arm64 GitHub Release clients with native authorization, atomic state, and launch proof; report signed-installer/store continuity separately when requested.
description: Windows child of the shared release contract; remains fail-closed until architecture-specific artifacts, PE verification, secure storage, installer lineage, and runtime evidence are complete.

title: Layout Management Foundation
goal: Establish one typed, transactional, adaptive layout authority that lets complete presentation profiles switch without changing client semantics or losing user state.
description: Platform-neutral parent for layout identity, catalog and resolution, preferences, preview/commit recovery, semantic destinations, state ownership, appearance composition, and desktop/mobile renderer contracts.

title: Desktop Layout Profiles
goal: Deliver complete workbench and studio desktop profiles with equivalent capabilities, distinct component systems, state-safe switching, and verified rebuild and launch.
description: Desktop renderer child of Layout Management Foundation; owns expanded/medium composition, keyboard/pointer behavior, desktop previews and goldens, complete shell migration, build, and launch.

title: Mobile Layout Profiles
goal: Deliver complete workbench and studio mobile profiles with conversation-first touch composition, lifecycle-safe switching, and independent Android/iOS verification.
description: Mobile renderer child of Layout Management Foundation; owns compact/medium composition, touch/lifecycle behavior, mobile previews and goldens, fixed-shell removal, and Android/iOS verification.

title: Catalog-Driven Layout Isolation
goal: Implement a cardinality-independent layout product in which N registered profiles across M declared runtime surfaces produce and validate exactly N×M mutually isolated bundles without changing the current designs.
description: Current delivery plan that supersedes fixed-count layout checkpoints. It owns catalog-derived composition, neutral runtime ports, profile-private renderers, transactional switching, dynamic verification, frozen-design evidence, desktop launch, and independent Android verification.

title: Isolated Renderer Completion
goal: Finish complete profile-private layout rendering and hard transitive isolation while preserving every current layout design exactly.
description: Child completion plan for neutral destination ports, disjoint profile renderer ownership, atomic shared-path removal, dynamic isolation gates, comparison-only visual restoration, per-Node commits, rebuild/open, and independent Android verification.
